title: Ctf18-dependent localization of interstitial telomeric sequence to nuclear pore complexes prevents chromosome fragility.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the 6,683,059-byte Zenodo ZIP (record 21459281, CC-BY-4.0) and extracted it: 94 files (51 .xlsx, 32 .rex, 6 .zpcr, 4 .pcrd, 1 ReadMe.txt) laid out one folder per paper figure. Opened all 51 spreadsheets with openpyxl and printed every sheet's dimensions; 2 of 51 are not valid xlsx and fail to open ('no item named [Content_Types].xml'). Dumped the contents of the five most table-like sheets: the chromosome-fragility colony counts (47x42), the zoning assay (6x17), a pooled ChEC-qPCR 'All 3 norm' sheet, the senescence time course, and a raw qPCR machine export. Largest single sheet in the whole deposit is 76 rows x 7 columns; the entire deposit is ~64,500 spreadsheet cells including blanks.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The biological conclusions (Ctf18/Mrc1/Scc2/Mms21 epistasis, Nup170 interaction, protection from homologous-recombination breakage) come from the paper text. The second Zenodo record (21458799, Southern blot PhosphorImage TIFFs) is a single 339,536,210-byte ZIP, over the 50 MB cap, so I read its metadata only and did not open the images. Europe PMC's supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out, so Supplementary Tables S1/S2 (yeast strain and primer lists) were not retrieved.

a1_downloadable.note: Both Zenodo records are open, CC-BY-4.0, no login. I downloaded and extracted the 6.7 MB source-data ZIP successfully.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no label column anywhere. Each figure panel is a hand-built spreadsheet with merged multi-row headers; the genotype is encoded in the folder name and sheet tab ('mrc1-AQ 1x3 clones'), not in a cell. Some headers are in French ('moyenne', 'Echantillon', 'Feuil1'). Any target would have to be constructed by hand from 51 differently shaped sheets.

a3_inputs_present.note: There are no model inputs. The only predictor available is a categorical yeast genotype with roughly a dozen levels (WT, ctf18, mrc1, mrc1-AQ, scc2-45, nup170, sir4, ku70, mms21-dC, pol2-K571R, mre11, rfa1-DY) plus a timepoint. No sequences, no genomic coordinates, no images paired with the scored outcomes.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated where they exist: qPCR 'Ct' and 'Calc Conc (copies/ul)', ChEC signal as a TG/ARO1 ratio, time in minutes, zoning as percent of nuclei per zone, fragility as percent white/red/sectorized colonies, senescence in population doublings over days.

a5_enough_rows.note: Far under the 1,500-row bar, and under the 400-row classification bar. Verified in the files: the fragility experiment is 12 clones (5 TG300-mod, 7 TG300) over ~10 plates; the zoning assay is 3 strains x 3 cell-cycle classes with 28-52 nuclei each; the pooled ChEC-qPCR sheets hold 4 timepoints x 2-5 clones per genotype, so on the order of 150-250 normalized values in total. The 6,410 numeric cells in the summary sheets are overwhelmingly per-well standards and replicate intermediates, not independent experimental units.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits; the 339 MB blot-image ZIP was not needed and was not downloaded.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing contradicts the paper: the folders map one-to-one onto Figures 2-7 and S1/S2/S7, and the ReadMe honestly flags one rfa1-G77E condition as collected but not published. There is no aggregate row count in the paper to check against.

a8_label_provenance.note: All values trace to physical measurements: quantitative PCR after chromatin endogenous cleavage, microscope scoring of nuclear zones, colony sectoring counts, and Southern blots. No model-derived or feature-derived labels.

honest_claim_h3: No honest modelling claim is available: with roughly a dozen yeast genotypes and a few hundred measurements, any model would be restating the paper's own bar charts.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use yeast genotype and cell-cycle timing to predict how strongly a chromosome site touches the nuclear pore.
plain_idea.train_on: What a model could see is a yeast strain's genotype (which repair or replication gene is deleted or mutated) plus a timepoint. I counted roughly 150-250 such measured conditions across the deposit, against a bar of 1,500.
plain_idea.predict: The output would be the chromatin endogenous cleavage signal, a quantitative-PCR ratio measuring how often a chromosomal site sits next to a nuclear pore protein, or the percentage of colonies showing chromosome breakage. Both are direct lab measurements.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: The biology matters to telomere and genome-stability labs, but the question is answered by the paper's own statistics; a model adds nothing at this sample size.

ml_idea: None viable. The only ideas the data supports are predicting the nuclear-pore contact signal or the chromosome-breakage rate from genotype, both of which are a dozen group means that the paper already reports with Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests and ANOVA. A separate idea, learning to quantify Southern blot bands from the 339 MB PhosphorImage TIFF archive, fails for want of labels: the images are deposited raw and unpaired with any annotation.

effort.compute_note: Measured, not estimated: the whole deposit is 6.7 MB and all 51 workbooks parse in seconds. The 12 hours is the hand-reshaping cost of 51 bespoke sheets with merged headers, genotypes living in folder names, and 2 corrupt files; it buys a table too small to model.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct genotype-by-clone-by-timepoint measurements in the pooled 'All norm' sheets. It is a few hundred, not a few thousand, and that ends it in ten minutes.

verdict_reason: Exemplary open data (CC-BY-4.0, raw plus processed, opened and verified) attached to a hypothesis-driven yeast genetics paper, but it is per-figure source data, not a dataset. Fails A5 on size (roughly 150-250 experimental units against a 1,500 bar), A2 because no label column exists across 51 hand-built spreadsheets, and A3 because the only input is a categorical genotype with about a dozen levels.
